title: Cannabis on a Budget: How to Shop Smart and Save
h1: Cannabis Budgeting: Smart Ways to Spend Less and Get More
metaDescription: Practical ways to save on cannabis without settling: what you're paying for, smart dispensary habits, value formats, stretching your stash and using rewards.
excerpt: Affordable cannabis is about cost per use, not the sticker price. Here's how to compare prices, pick value formats, make a stash last, and put rewards and deals to work.
keyTakeaways: Compare price per gram, or per milligram of THC for edibles, and remember Michigan adds a 10% excise tax and 6% sales tax to adult-use purchases.
THC percentage is only part of value; freshness, aroma and how you actually use a product matter as much.
Smalls, shake, multipacks, cartridges and multi-dose edibles often cost less per use than premium eighths.
The Society, High Society's rewards program, is free to join and earns points on qualifying purchases; check the deals page before you shop.
Store flower airtight, use a little less, and set a monthly number so cannabis fits your budget.
body:
A cannabis budget works best when you pay for what you'll actually notice. Compare price per gram, or per milligram of THC for edibles, check the deals page before you go, join a free rewards program, and lean on value formats like smalls, shake and multipacks. Then make it last with good storage, smaller doses and a monthly number you stick to. Affordable cannabis is about cost per use, not the lowest sticker price.

## What you're paying for: potency is only part of value

A dispensary price tag reflects a lot more than THC. Some of what goes into it:

- **How it was grown.** Indoor flower generally costs more to produce than greenhouse or outdoor flower.
- **Bud size and looks.** Big, dense, photogenic buds sell at a premium, while the plant's smaller buds often sell for less.
- **Brand and packaging.** Well-known names, glass jars and limited drops carry a markup.
- **Labor.** Hand-trimmed flower and small-batch extracts take more work.
- **Potency.** Higher THC numbers usually come with higher prices.

THC is the number most people shop by, but it's a rough guide. Michigan labels note that actual THC and CBD values may vary by 10%, so a couple of percentage points won't necessarily change your experience. How a product was grown, dried and stored, plus your own tolerance, shapes a session as much as the headline number. Paying for the top of the THC range only makes sense if you'll feel the difference.

## Value beyond THC: terpenes, freshness, effect

Three things decide whether a purchase was worth it:

- **Terpenes.** These aroma compounds give a strain its smell and flavor. If you love a citrusy or piney strain, a budget pick with a nose you enjoy beats a pricier one you don't.
- **Freshness.** Michigan labels list the harvest date. Older flower dries out and loses aroma, so a fresh budget eighth can beat a stale premium one.
- **Effect.** The best value cannabis for you is the product that does what you want at a dose you like. Note what works, and buy it again.

Try a small size before committing to a big one. A gram or an eighth is a cheap experiment; an ounce of something you don't enjoy isn't.

## Smart habits: compare per-gram prices, watch promos, ask questions, size up

### Do the per-gram math

Divide the price by the grams to compare sizes and products fairly. Here's how it works with round example prices, used only to show the math:

| Size | Grams | Example price | Price per gram |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gram | 1 | $10 | $10.00 |
| Eighth | 3.5 | $25 | $7.14 |
| Quarter | 7 | $45 | $6.43 |
| Half ounce | 14 | $80 | $5.71 |
| Ounce | 28 | $140 | $5.00 |

For edibles, divide the price by the total milligrams of THC in the package. For ounce and gram conversions, see [grams in an ounce, explained](/blog/how-many-grams-ounce-marijuana/), then come back to the math.

### Watch promos

Dispensary deals change often, so look at the current offers before each trip, and know that The Society gives members access to some online-only sales. When you check in at one of our stores, you can share your phone number and email to hear about discounts and special offers.

### Ask questions

Our budtenders can point you to value options, explain the difference between two similar products, and help you read a label's harvest date and THC numbers. Ask what's new, what's a good value right now, and what regulars come back for.

### Size up, within the limits

Bigger sizes usually cost less per gram, so once you know what you like, sizing up can pay off. Michigan allows up to 2.5 ounces per transaction, with no more than 15 grams of it as concentrate, and anything over 2.5 ounces kept at home has to be locked up. Michigan also adds a 10% excise tax and 6% sales tax to adult-use purchases, with sales tax figured on the price plus the excise tax, so check whether a price includes tax.

## Budget-friendly formats: concentrates, vapes, pre-rolls, multi-dose edibles, shake and smalls

Some formats stretch a dollar further than others:

| Format | Why it can be good value | Watch for |
|---|---|---|
| Smalls (popcorn buds) | Same plant as the big buds, just smaller, often for less | Can dry out faster; check the harvest date |
| Shake and mixed buds | The most wallet-friendly flower, good for rolling or cooking | Can be harsher; quality varies by batch |
| 1 g pre-rolls and multipacks | Often less per pre-roll than singles; no gear needed | Check whether they're filled with whole flower or shake |
| Vape cartridges | Easy to take one puff at a time; one battery serves many cartridges | The battery is an upfront cost |
| Disposable vapes | Cheap to try, no battery to buy | You pay for new hardware every time |
| Entry-level concentrates | Potent, so a small amount lasts | For experienced users; start very small |
| Multi-dose edibles | Easy to split into servings and compare by the milligram | Slow onset makes overdoing it easy |

Budget pre-rolls are a smart way to sample a strain before buying a bigger size, and a budget disposable vape works the same way for vapes. With edibles, Michigan caps an adult-use serving at 10 mg of THC and a package at 200 mg, so price per milligram is easy to work out. For the flower side, see [bud vs. shake vs. popcorn](/blog/cannabis-bud-vs-shake-vs-popcorn/).

## Value tier vs. top shelf: is cheap weed worth it?

Often, yes. Here's what you might give up with value-tier cannabis: bag appeal, since buds can be smaller or less uniform, some aroma intensity, batch-to-batch consistency, and the newest named drops.

What you don't give up is the basics. Whether a product is a value pick or top shelf, we work with trusted vendors, and what we bring in has passed Michigan's testing standards. A value product can still be fresh, flavorful and exactly what you wanted.

### Value weed brands and how to judge them

Some brands offer a value line alongside their premium one. Judge them the way you'd judge anything else: check the harvest date, look for intact, sticky buds rather than dry dust, and buy a small amount first. Cheap and good aren't opposites; stale and good are.

When is the upgrade worth it? Think special occasions, flavor-focused sessions where aroma is the point, or a product type you're trying for the first time. It's also worth it when a premium pick simply does something for you that a value one doesn't. For more on top-shelf flower, see our [premium flower guide](/blog/premium-cannabis-flower-guide/).

## Stretch your stash: storage, DIY edibles from trim, the right gear, lower doses, mixing

- **Store it right.** Keep flower in an airtight glass jar, somewhere cool and dark, away from heat and sunlight. Dry, crumbly flower burns fast and tastes harsh, which is money lost.
- **Cook with trim and shake.** Shake, trim and the last bits in the jar can become cannabutter or infused oil. Heat the cannabis first (decarboxylation) so it works in food. Any homemade edible's strength is an estimate, since THC per serving depends on the starting material's potency and on losses during heating and infusing. Start with a small piece, wait, label everything, and keep it away from children and pets.
- **Use the right gear.** A grinder gives an even burn. A dry-herb vaporizer can make flower go further: in a 2018 Johns Hopkins study, the same THC dose produced stronger effects vaporized than smoked. A small pipe or one-hitter keeps doses small.
- **Use a little less.** Smaller amounts, used less often, stretch any stash. Regular use builds tolerance, and time off can reverse it: in a brain-imaging study of daily users, the receptors THC acts on returned to normal levels after about four weeks without cannabis.
- **Mix it.** Stretch a pricier strain by blending it with shake or a lower-THC flower in a bowl or joint.

## Using loyalty points and the deals page

A dispensary loyalty program and a good promotion are the easiest savings, and they cost nothing to use.

**The Society.** Our rewards program is free to join, in store or online. Every qualifying purchase earns points automatically, and you can trade them for discounts or rewards at checkout, in store or online, with our team's help. Members get perks like exclusive discounts, personalized offers and early access to new and limited-edition products, plus special pricing and birthday rewards. Points may not apply to certain promotions or products, so ask at checkout. Join The Society on our [club member program page](/club-member-program/).

**The deals page.** Check our [deals page](/deals/) before each trip, and pair a deal with your points where that's allowed.

**Order ahead.** Browsing the online menu and ordering for pickup lets you compare prices calmly before you commit, and members of The Society get access to some online-only promotions. Our [guide to dispensary rewards programs](/blog/guide-to-cannabis-dispensary-rewards-programs/) explains how these programs compare from store to store.

## A simple monthly cannabis budget

1. **Set a number.** Pick a monthly amount that fits comfortably after bills and savings.
2. **Estimate your use.** Count sessions per week and roughly how much each one takes.
3. **Match formats to habits.** Smalls or shake for frequent use, a premium eighth for weekends, a multi-dose edible for nights in.
4. **Add tax.** Michigan's 10% excise tax plus 6% sales tax means a $100 adult-use purchase comes to $116.60.
5. **Plan your trips.** Fewer, planned purchases make it easier to catch deals and earn points.
6. **Track it.** Note what you bought, what it cost and whether you'd buy it again.

Here's the tax math in practice. If your all-in monthly budget is $120, aim for about $103 in products before tax, since $103 plus both taxes comes to about $120. Revisit the number after a month or two, once you know your real habits.

21+ only. Please consume responsibly.

faq.q: How can I save money on cannabis?
faq.a: Compare price per gram, check the deals page before you shop, join a free rewards program like The Society, and choose value formats such as smalls, shake or multipacks. Then make your purchase last: store flower airtight, use a little less and cook with leftover shake. Sizing up can lower the per-gram price, within Michigan's 2.5-ounce transaction limit.

Often, yes. Value-tier flower may have smaller buds, less aroma or more batch-to-batch variation, but it can still be fresh and enjoyable. Check the harvest date, look the product over, and buy a small amount first. Save premium purchases for when you'll notice the difference, like flavor-focused sessions or special occasions.

faq.q: Which cannabis products last longest for the money?
faq.a: Formats you can dose in small amounts usually stretch furthest: a vape cartridge on a reusable battery, a multi-dose edible package split into servings, or a small amount of concentrate for experienced users. For flower, smalls and shake cost less per gram, and good storage keeps them from drying out and going to waste.

faq.q: Is High Society's loyalty program free?
faq.a: Yes. Joining The Society is free, in store or online, and every qualifying purchase earns points automatically. You can redeem points for discounts or rewards at checkout, in store or online. Points may not apply to certain promotions or products, so ask our team at checkout if you're unsure how a reward applies.

faq.q: When do dispensaries run their best deals?
faq.a: It varies by store. Many dispensaries run promotions around holidays and big shopping days, and some offer member-only or online-only deals. The simplest approach is to check the deals page before each trip, share your phone number and email at check-in to hear about offers, and keep your rewards account active so you're ready when a promotion fits.

review.writerNotes: Low-risk article. No current deals, prices, point values, tier names or thresholds; the per-gram table uses labelled round example prices only. The app is not mentioned (dead App Store link); the brief's 'loyalty points, the app and the deals page' item is covered as rewards, the deals page and online ordering.
